title: 29 CFR 2560.503-1 — Claims procedure
jurisdiction: ERISA employee benefit plans; group-health subsections only
verified_summary: Group-health claimants receive at least 180 days after receipt to appeal; relevant claim records are available free on request. A single-level post-service appeal ordinarily has a 60-day decision limit; two levels and multiemployer exceptions differ.
why_it_matters: Protect appeal rights; do not use bill due date as appeal deadline.
limitations: Summary only; no complete archived source snapshot. Recheck before live use.

title: 29 CFR 2590.716-5 — Non-emergency surprise bills
jurisdiction: Applicable group health plans, including this synthetic ERISA plan
verified_summary: Covered non-emergency services from nonparticipating providers during visits to participating facilities receive specified cost-sharing protections. Cost sharing uses the recognized amount; the provider payment rate is a separate quantity.
why_it_matters: Primary plan-side authority for anesthesia dispute.
effective_or_updated: Plan years beginning on or after 2022-01-01
limitations: Summary only; no complete archived source snapshot. Recheck before live use.

title: 45 CFR 149.420 — Provider balance billing
jurisdiction: Nonparticipating providers at participating qualifying facilities under applicable private coverage
verified_summary: Providers cannot impose more than protected cost sharing for qualifying covered services. The notice-and-consent exception is unavailable for anesthesiology. Provider notification to the plan about the participating facility is addressed separately.
why_it_matters: A generic consent form does not defeat this anesthesia argument.
effective_or_updated: Services during plan/policy years beginning on or after 2022-01-01
limitations: Summary only; no complete archived source snapshot. Recheck before live use.

title: 29 CFR 2590.715-2719 — Internal appeals and external review
jurisdiction: Applicable group-health internal/external review framework; verify grandfathering and route
verified_summary: Federal external review includes surprise-billing compliance disputes; the regulation illustrates anesthesia at participating facilities. The federal filing window is four months after receipt of the relevant adverse notice, with calendar exceptions; exhaustion normally matters.
why_it_matters: Potential later escalation, not automatic immediate submission. No final internal denial exists in the demo.
limitations: Summary only; no complete archived source snapshot. Recheck before live use.
